"""studio - JMS CURATE stage: file-based accept/reject/edit + training split.

The curation surface is entirely FILE-based — no per-row graph nodes. Two files
under <project>/dataset/ carry the state:

- raw.jsonl   — the generator's output (immutable here; owned by jms_gen). Each
  line is `{"_id","_type","_meta":{"chunks":[...],"job":...},"messages":[...]}`.
- decisions.jsonl — an append-only OVERLAY this module owns. Each line is
  `{"_id","action":"accept"|"reject"|"edit","messages":[...](edit only),"ts"}`.
  The LAST entry per `_id` wins; earlier ones are history. `materialize` compacts
  the file (rewrites deduped) before building the split.

A row's effective status merges the two: no decision → "pending"; else the last
decision's action → accepted / rejected / edited. `edited` is its own stats
bucket but is treated as accepted-with-edit at materialize (its edited content
wins over raw). `materialize` carves accepted+edited rows deterministically into
dataset/train.jsonl + dataset/holdout.jsonl by a sha1(_id)%100 hash gate, and
strips EVERY underscore-prefixed key (_id/_type/_meta) so the shipped rows are
pure sft-chat `{"messages":[...]}`.

Kept out of jms_projects (which stays graph-only) and out of jms_gen (the
generation engine); imports `validate_row` from jms_gen for edit validation and
`_find_project`/`jms_project_dir`/`_count_lines` from jms_projects. No circular
import: neither of those imports this module.

Checker notes (jaclang 0.16.1): dict values are `any` → int(str(...)); never a
local named `root` (graph builtin); slice + splitlines for pagination.
"""

import json;
import os;
import hashlib;
import datetime;
import from pathlib { Path }
import from jms_gen { validate_row }
import from jms_projects { JmsProject, _find_project, jms_project_dir, _count_lines }

def _now() -> str { ... }

# ------------------------------------------------------------- file helpers ----
def _dataset_dir(p: JmsProject) -> Path { ... }

def _raw_file(p: JmsProject) -> Path { ... }

def _decisions_file(p: JmsProject) -> Path { ... }

def _train_file(p: JmsProject) -> Path { ... }

def _holdout_file(p: JmsProject) -> Path { ... }

"""Every non-blank JSONL line of raw.jsonl parsed to a dict (garbage lines
skipped). O(total) — acceptable at this product's row counts."""
def _read_raw(p: JmsProject) -> list[dict] { ... }

"""decisions.jsonl folded to {_id: last-decision-dict} — last line per id wins,
so a re-decide simply appends and this read picks the newest."""
def _read_decisions(p: JmsProject) -> dict { ... }

"""Effective status of *rid* given the folded decisions map."""
def _status_of(rid: str, decisions: dict) -> str { ... }

"""Write *text* to *dst* atomically: a per-pid sibling `.tmp` in the same directory,
then os.replace (an atomic rename on a POSIX filesystem). A reader either sees the
whole old file or the whole new one — never a truncated one — and a crash mid-write
leaves the previous contents intact instead of a half file."""
def _atomic_write(dst: Path, text: str) -> None { ... }

"""Append one decision line, normalising a missing trailing newline first so the
overlay never runs two records together on one line.

A REAL append (open "a"), not read-all-then-rewrite-all: the previous version
rebuilt the entire decision history on every accept/reject click, so a crash
mid-write truncated every decision the user had ever made. The trailing-newline
probe reads exactly one byte via st_size + seek instead of the whole file.
# ponytail: ceiling — O_APPEND makes each write atomic against other appenders on
# a local filesystem; two servers appending at once interleave records but never
# corrupt one. Cross-machine (NFS) appends are out of scope for a one-GPU box."""
def _append_decisions(p: JmsProject, added: str) -> None { ... }

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ readers ----
"""One row as the client lists it: id/type/status + the effective messages
(edited version when edited) + chunk provenance + source job id."""
def _row_view(row: dict, rid: str, st: str, decisions: dict) -> dict { ... }

"""Curation counters for the header tiles. `acceptance_pct` = (accepted+edited)
over all DECIDED rows (pending excluded); 0 when nothing is decided. train/holdout
are line counts of the materialized files, 0 before the first BUILD."""
def curate_stats(pid: str) -> dict { ... }

"""curate_stats over ALREADY-LOADED raw rows + folded decisions. Same dict, same
key order — the decide_* endpoints reuse the data they just read instead of
re-parsing raw.jsonl and decisions.jsonl a second and third time per click."""
def _stats_from(p: JmsProject, raw: list[dict], decisions: dict) -> dict { ... }

"""A page of merged rows for *filter* (all|pending|accepted|rejected|edited),
sliced [offset:offset+cap] (cap 100). `total` is the count for THIS filter."""
def curate_rows(pid: str, offset: int, limit: int, `filter: str = "all") -> dict { ... }

# --------------------------------------------------------------- decisions -----
"""Record one accept/reject/edit/reset for *row_id*. `edit` requires a valid
sft-chat `messages` list (jms_gen.validate_row). Returns the fresh curate_stats,
or {"error": ...}.

`reset` is the UNDO action: the overlay is append-only/last-write-wins, so undoing
is just another decision whose action `_status_of` does not recognise — it falls
through to "pending", which is exactly what undo means here. Nothing else needed
changing: `materialize` already skips pending rows and `rejected_ids` already only
collects rejects."""
def decide_row(pid: str, row_id: str, action: str, messages: list = []) -> dict { ... }

"""Bulk accept or reject a set of row ids in one append (unknown ids are
skipped). Returns the fresh curate_stats, or {"error": ...}."""
def decide_page(pid: str, row_ids: list[str], action: str) -> dict { ... }

"""_ids of every currently-rejected row (feeds the REGENERATE button)."""
def rejected_ids(pid: str) -> list[str] { ... }

# -------------------------------------------------------------- materialize ----
"""Rewrite decisions.jsonl deduped (one line per id, last-decision wins)."""
def _compact_decisions(p: JmsProject, decisions: dict) -> None { ... }

"""The final shipped form of one accepted/edited row: edited messages win, then
EVERY underscore-prefixed key (_id/_type/_meta) is dropped → pure sft-chat."""
def _final_row(row: dict, rid: str, st: str, decisions: dict) -> dict { ... }

"""Compact the overlay, then build the training split from accepted+edited rows
(edited content wins, underscore keys stripped). Deterministic carve:
sha1(_id)%100 < holdout_pct → holdout, else train. Writes dataset/train.jsonl +
dataset/holdout.jsonl. Returns {train_rows, holdout_rows, skipped_rejected,
skipped_pending}.

REFUSES a no-op build: with nothing accepted or edited there is no split to make,
and the two writes below would replace an existing train.jsonl + holdout.jsonl
with EMPTY files. It returns {"error": ...} before either write instead of
reporting a useless `train 0 · holdout 0`."""
def materialize(pid: str, holdout_pct: int = 10) -> dict { ... }

The JMS product surface (frontend → JmsShell → JmsProject) is backed by a small

root, so every read (`[root -->][?:JmsProject]`) is multi-tenant isolated for
free — same guarantee persistence.sv.jac / evals.sv.jac rely on.

A project owns an on-disk skeleton under <workspace_root>/jms-projects/<slug>/
(dataset/ sources/ jobs/ runs/ evals/); the slug is the filesystem identity and
is **immutable after creation** — `rename_project` changes the DISPLAY name only
and never touches the directory (see its docstring for why). Sources are
fast os.walk stat passes — no file contents read — producing file counts + a
bytes//4 token estimate + an extension histogram, capped at 50k files.

`write_project_snapshot` dumps project.json into the project dir for the later
generate/train workers to consume.

Lifecycle extras (all additive — every pre-existing signature/return shape is
untouched): `rename_project` (display name), `duplicate_project` (config-only
clone by default, opt-in streamed curated-dataset copy), `dataset_export_info`
(cheap size probe), `export_dataset` (paginated JSONL reader under a hard
per-response byte budget) and `export_summary` (config + counts + results as
JSON or Markdown, capped and self-reporting when it caps).

Checker notes (jaclang 0.16.1): `++>` returns a LIST — unwrap `(root ++> X())[0]`;
dict values are `any`, so `int(str(...))` when coercing; import native symbols
directly. os.walk dir pruning is done via list.clear()+extend (in-place, no slice
assignment). jobs.safe() gates the slug so it is always a shell/path-safe token.

"""CurateStage — the CURATE stage panel of a JMS project.

Reviews the generator's raw.jsonl rows one page at a time and records an
accept / reject / edit decision on each (server-side file overlay), then carves
the accepted+edited rows into a deterministic train/holdout split.

Header: stat tiles (GENERATED / PENDING / ACCEPTED / REJECTED / EDITED / ACC %,
plus TRAIN / HOLDOUT once a split is built). Filter chips scope the list to one
status. Each row is a status dot + _type chip + first-user-message excerpt with
an expand toggle; expanded shows the full role-labeled transcript, its chunk
provenance, and ✓ ACCEPT / ✗ REJECT / EDIT actions (EDIT swaps in a per-message
textarea → SAVE / CANCEL). A bulk bar accepts every pending row on the page and
fires a REGENERATE-REJECTED gen job (jms_gen.start_gen with regen_of); the footer
builds the split via materialize (two-click confirm when a split already exists).

KEYBOARD REVIEW (this is the stage a user spends hours in, so it is driveable
without the mouse): j/↓ and k/↑ move a cursor down/up the page, ↵ expands, a
accepts, r rejects, e opens the inline editor, u undoes. The keydown
listener is registered in a useEffect (NOT `can with exit` — that cleanup would
capture first-render state) and every handler bails when the event target is an
input/textarea/select/contentEditable or carries a Meta/Ctrl/Alt modifier, so
typing in the edit textarea or the holdout field is never hijacked.

# ponytail: the cursor is a plain int index into the current page, not a row id.
# Ceiling — it does not survive a page turn or a filter change (both reset it to
# 0), and if a decision shortens `rows` under it, it clamps to the last row rather
# than tracking "the row I was on". Correct for the actual workflow (review a page
# top-to-bottom, turn the page) and it costs no id-to-index lookup per keystroke.

UNDO (`u`) is just another decision on that same append-only overlay: it appends
action `reset`, which is the one action jms_curate._status_of does not recognise,
so the row falls through to "pending" — exactly what undo means here. It takes the
identical doDecide path as a/r, so the stat tiles, the progress bar and the stage
rail all refresh the same way. An already-pending row is skipped client-side
rather than round-tripped: the server would accept it happily, but a request that
provably changes nothing should not be sent, and the UI should not flicker as if
something happened.

`project` is the get_project() dict (pid + provider/model + gen_jobs); `onRefresh`
re-pulls it after a mutation so the stage rail's curate dot updates. Handlers are
named pick.../do.../build.../move... — never set<HasVar>."""

"""Hand-authored editorial seed videos so the generated mode works without an LLM key.
Each segment is one scene; scene start words are computed from segment lengths."""

import from services.ai { Script, SceneSpec }

obj Segment {
    has text: str,
        scene: SceneSpec;
}

obj SeedVideo {
    has topic: str,
        title: str,
        summary: str,
        segments: list[Segment],
        citations: list[str],
        quiz_question: str,
        quiz_choices: list[str],
        quiz_answer: int,
        quiz_explanation: str,
        tags: list[str];

    def to_script -> Script {
        parts: list[str] = [];
        scenes: list[SceneSpec] = [];
        n = 0;
        for seg in self.segments {
            seg.scene.start_word = n;
            scenes.append(seg.scene);
            parts.append(seg.text.strip());
            n += len(seg.text.split());
        }
        return Script(
            title=self.title,
            summary=self.summary,
            narration=" ".join(parts),
            scenes=scenes,
            citations=self.citations,
            quiz_question=self.quiz_question,
            quiz_choices=self.quiz_choices,
            quiz_answer=self.quiz_answer,
            quiz_explanation=self.quiz_explanation,
            tags=self.tags
        );
    }
}

def _s(template: str, heading: str = "", body: str = "", items: list[str] = [], labels: list[str] = [],
       values: list[float] = [], image_query: str = "") -> SceneSpec {
    return SceneSpec(
        template=template, start_word=0, heading=heading, body=body, items=items, labels=labels,
        values=values, image_query=image_query
    );
}

  opts:    dict  env-var overrides (filtered by the method's env_keys)

import paths;
import workspace;

# supplies ({base_model}/{output_dir}/{config_yaml} — train.sv.jac only passes

"""Env keys for *method* — method env_keys, else train.sft_keys/dpo_keys."""

def log_parser_for(backend_name: str, method: str) -> str { ... }

"""List configured backends + their methods (for UI / debug). Unwired stub
backends (_STUB_BACKENDS) are omitted — their templates can't be rendered into a

"""studio - JMS project management + source scanning (OSP graph, per-user).

The JMS product surface (frontend → JmsShell → JmsProject) is backed by a small
graph: `root ++> JmsProject ++> JmsSource`. Projects hang off the caller's OWN
root, so every read (`[root -->][?:JmsProject]`) is multi-tenant isolated for
free — same guarantee persistence.sv.jac / evals.sv.jac rely on.

A project owns an on-disk skeleton under <workspace_root>/jms-projects/<slug>/
(dataset/ sources/ jobs/ runs/ evals/); the slug is the filesystem identity and
is **immutable after creation** — `rename_project` changes the DISPLAY name only
and never touches the directory (see its docstring for why). Sources are
fast os.walk stat passes — no file contents read — producing file counts + a
bytes//4 token estimate + an extension histogram, capped at 50k files.

`write_project_snapshot` dumps project.json into the project dir for the later
generate/train workers to consume.

Lifecycle extras (all additive — every pre-existing signature/return shape is
untouched): `rename_project` (display name), `duplicate_project` (config-only
clone by default, opt-in streamed curated-dataset copy), `dataset_export_info`
(cheap size probe), `export_dataset` (paginated JSONL reader under a hard
per-response byte budget) and `export_summary` (config + counts + results as
JSON or Markdown, capped and self-reporting when it caps).

Checker notes (jaclang 0.16.1): `++>` returns a LIST — unwrap `(root ++> X())[0]`;
dict values are `any`, so `int(str(...))` when coercing; import native symbols
directly. os.walk dir pruning is done via list.clear()+extend (in-place, no slice
assignment). jobs.safe() gates the slug so it is always a shell/path-safe token.
"""

import json;
import os;
import shutil;
import fnmatch;
import datetime;
import jobs;
import paths;
import from pathlib { Path }
import from uuid { uuid4 }

def _now() -> str { ... }

# --------------------------------------------------------------- scan config ---
glob _EX_DIRS: list[str] = [".git", "node_modules", "dist", "build", ".venv", "__pycache__", ".jac"];
glob _BINARY_EXT: list[str] = [
    ".png", ".jpg", ".jpeg", ".gif", ".webp", ".ico", ".bmp", ".tiff", ".svg",
    ".pdf", ".zip", ".gz", ".tar", ".tgz", ".bz2", ".xz", ".7z", ".rar",
    ".exe", ".dll", ".bin", ".so", ".dylib", ".o", ".a", ".class", ".jar",
    ".woff", ".woff2", ".ttf", ".otf", ".eot",
    ".mp4", ".mp3", ".wav", ".mov", ".avi", ".mkv", ".flac", ".ogg",
    ".pyc", ".pyo", ".db", ".sqlite", ".sqlite3", ".npy", ".npz", ".safetensors", ".gguf"
];
glob _INC_CODE: list[str] = [".py", ".js", ".ts", ".tsx", ".jac", ".go", ".rs", ".java", ".c", ".cpp", ".h", ".md"];
glob _INC_DOCS: list[str] = [".md", ".rst", ".txt", ".mdx"];
glob _MAX_BYTES: int = 1048576;   # 1 MB — skip larger files
glob _MAX_FILES: int = 50000;     # walk cap — bail with a note beyond this

# ------------------------------------------------------------- export budget ---
# HARD per-response ceiling for `export_dataset` / `export_summary`. A curated
# dataset is unbounded (tens of MB is normal), and one endpoint in this repo once
# shipped 48 x 4MB base64 blobs in a single response — so the reader is PAGINATED
# and every response says, in-band, whether it stopped early (`eof` / `truncated`
# / `note`). Nothing is ever silently dropped.
glob _EXPORT_MAX_BYTES: int = 2000000;   # ~2 MB of JSONL text per response
glob _EXPORT_MAX_LINES: int = 2000;      # …or 2k rows, whichever trips first
glob _SUMMARY_MAX_ITEMS: int = 200;      # per-list cap inside export_summary
glob _COPY_CHUNK: int = 1048576;         # 1 MB streaming-copy chunk

# ------------------------------------------------------------------- views -----
"""One project as a card sees it: fields + a derived source count."""
obj JmsProjectView {
    has pid: str = "",
        name: str = "",
        slug: str = "",
        use_case: str = "",
        created: str = "",
        provider: str = "claude",
        model: str = "claude-sonnet-5",
        source_count: int = 0,
        group_id: str = "";
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------- nodes -----
node JmsProject {
    has pid: str = "",
        name: str = "",
        slug: str = "",
        use_case: str = "",
        created: str = "",
        provider: str = "claude",
        model: str = "claude-sonnet-5",
        group_id: str = "";
}

node JmsSource {
    has sid: str = "",
        kind: str = "code",           # code | docs
        path: str = "",
        include: list[str] = [],
        exclude: list[str] = [],
        files: int = 0,
        est_tokens: int = 0,
        skipped: int = 0,
        ext_json: str = "",           # JSON dict {ext: count} — top-8 histogram
        scanned_at: str = "";
}

"""A GENERATE-stage dataset plan draft/approval, child of a JmsProject
(`project ++> JmsGenPlan`). The plan body itself is opaque JSON in `plan_json`
(shape: description/schema/mix/target_rows/system_prompt/grounding_notes) —
authored + mutated by jms_plan.sv.jac, which imports this type. Kept HERE (not in
jms_plan) so get_project can read plans without a circular import back into
jms_plan (which imports jms_projects). `version` is monotonic per project; at
most one plan is `approved` at a time."""
node JmsGenPlan {
    has version: int = 1,
        status: str = "draft",        # draft | approved
        provider: str = "",           # claude | mlx
        model: str = "",
        plan_json: str = "",
        created: str = "",
        approved_at: str = "";
}

"""A SYNTHESIZE-stage generation job, child of a JmsProject
(`project ++> JmsGenJob`). Mirrors the on-disk job under
<project>/jobs/<jid>/ (job.json / run.log / progress.json) — the FILES are the
live source of truth (they survive server restarts); the node is the graph
index get_project lists from, with rows_done/est_cost_usd/finished synced on
terminal transitions by jms_gen.sv.jac gen_status. Kept HERE (not in jms_gen)
for the same one-way-import reason as JmsGenPlan: get_project reads jobs
without importing jms_gen (which imports jms_projects)."""
node JmsGenJob {
    has jid: str = "",
        status: str = "running",      # running | completed | failed | stopped
        provider: str = "",           # claude | mlx
        model: str = "",
        target_rows: int = 0,
        max_rows: int = 0,
        plan_version: int = 1,
        est_cost_usd: float = 0.0,
        rows_done: int = 0,
        regen_of_json: str = "[]",
        started: str = "",
        finished: str = "",
        error: str = "";
}

"""A TRAIN-stage finetuning run, child of a JmsProject (`project ++> JmsTrainRun`).
Two backends: `local-mlx` (mlx_lm.lora LoRA under runs/<rid>/, jobs-engine
detached, one at a time behind the GLOBAL heavy GPU lock) and `spheron` (a remote
Spheron VM run delegated to cloudruns.sv.jac — the CloudRun node owns the VM
lifecycle; this node just carries `cloud_run_id` to proxy status through). Kept
HERE (not in jms_train) for the same one-way-import reason as JmsGenPlan/JmsGenJob:
get_project reads runs without importing jms_train (which imports jms_projects).
Live status + terminal node sync are jms_train.sv.jac train_status's job; the node
fields are the restart-surviving graph index. `adapter_path` is the local dir
mlx_lm writes / cloudruns pulls the adapter into. `cfg_json` snapshots the opts."""
node JmsTrainRun {
    has rid: str = "",
        backend: str = "local-mlx",   # local-mlx | spheron
        base_model: str = "",
        status: str = "running",      # running | completed | failed | stopped
        cfg_json: str = "",
        adapter_path: str = "",
        cloud_run_id: str = "",
        started: str = "",
        finished: str = "";
}

"""An EVAL-stage scoring run over a project's holdout, child of a JmsProject
(`project ++> JmsEvalRun`). Scores a completed local-mlx train run's adapter on
the materialized dataset/holdout.jsonl via a detached worker
(scripts/jms_eval_worker.jac) — the on-disk evals/<eid>/ dir (outputs.jsonl /
scores.jsonl / summary.json + the jobs-engine job.json/run.log) is the
restart-surviving source of truth; the node is the graph index synced on terminal
transitions by jms_eval.sv.jac eval_status. Kept HERE (not in jms_eval) for the
same one-way-import reason as JmsGenJob/JmsTrainRun: get_project lists evals
without importing jms_eval (which imports jms_projects). `metric` is judge (Claude
LLM-as-judge, 1-5) or similarity (difflib ratio → 1-5); mean_score/pass_rate/n are
filled from summary.json on completion."""
node JmsEvalRun {
    has eid: str = "",
        run_rid: str = "",
        metric: str = "judge",        # judge | similarity
        status: str = "running",      # running | completed | failed | stopped
        n: int = 0,
        mean_score: float = 0.0,
        pass_rate: float = 0.0,
        started: str = "",
        finished: str = "",
        error: str = "";
}

"""<workspace_root>/jms-projects/<slug> — the project's on-disk home."""
def jms_project_dir(slug: str) -> Path { ... }

"""Non-blank JSONL line count, 0 on missing/unreadable file."""

provider swaps the drawer body for an inline "Connect <Provider>" key-entry
screen (saving via `set_anthropic_key`/`set_openai_key`, mirroring
`ApiKeyModal.cl.jac`) instead of disabling the chip. Once configured the body
switches back to the normal thread + composer.

`"assistant"` workspace, same shape `sections/Chat.cl.jac` uses for the main
chat surface — a togglable history list (newest first) with new/open/delete,
so an assistant conversation survives a page reload.

raw-fetch-reader pattern `Chat.cl.jac` uses for `/function/chat_stream` (same
SSE frame protocol: `load`/`token`/`done`/`error`, plus the jaclang

sends instead of closing the socket — miss it and the reader hangs forever).
